kit.sidebar.title: Places
ask.approve-with-passkey: Approving asks for your passkey, which also opens this wallet. Nothing else is asked of you unless a check this wallet makes after that fails or warns, and then it says why here.
ask.passkey-again: Nothing was sent. Use the button above to try your passkey again, or Decline.
ask.who.origin: This page actually came from {origin}. Your browser told this wallet that, not the request.
ask.who.purpose: Why they say they want it: {purpose}
ask.wallet.opens: Opens {wallet}, the wallet that answers this page.
ask.wallet.choose-why: This browser holds {count} wallets. The one you choose answers this page from now on, and only its passkey is asked for.
ask.wallet.gone-title: The wallet that signed in here is not in this browser
ask.wallet.gone: The wallet that last signed in to {origin} from this browser is no longer held here. Choose the wallet to answer with. A company's key is made from the wallet that gives it, so another wallet's key opens nothing the first one saved.
ask.warn.given: You can refuse the next time they ask. Whoever is behind that page keeps everything they have already opened and anything they copied while it was open, and nothing can take back a key.
ask.warn.how-long: Their page holds the key while it is open, and this wallet never stores it. Nothing stops them keeping their own copy, and nothing here could tell. Treat this as given for good.
ask.sign-in.headline: Sign in to {origin}
ask.sign-in.lede: Tells {origin} this wallet's public address and proves you hold it. Anyone on the network can read what is paid to and from that address. Nothing else about you is sent.
ask.sign-in.warn: {origin} will keep a signed statement that you were here, and the address it was signed by. This wallet can stop signing you in to them later. Nothing can take back what has gone.
ask.unlock.headline: Let {origin} open a company's records
ask.unlock.lede: Gives {origin} the key to the records this company keeps for you. Their page can open those records whenever it is open, and this wallet cannot watch it happen. It also lets the page check whether a payslip was paid to one of your wallets; it does not tell the page any of your addresses.
ask.unlock.compare: the person who invited you to this company gave you themselves, and not through this page
ask.keyring.headline: Let {origin} use the keys saved under the account name it gives
ask.keyring.lede: Those keys open the records of, and approve payments for, every company you belong to on that site - not only one. Whoever runs that page can use them whenever it is open, and this wallet cannot watch it happen.
ask.keyring.person: The account name the page gives you: {person}. Any page can give any name; this wallet can only show it to you.
ask.keyring.signed-in-as: The page says you signed in to it as {address}. This wallet checks that address is one of its own before it gives anything.
ask.keyring.new-company: The page is setting up a new company, with you as its founding signer. This wallet makes up the company's label itself and gives it with your keys for it. Give them only if you are setting this company up yourself, on this page, now.
ask.balance.headline: Pay into a company vault for {origin}
ask.balance.headline-public: Pay publicly into a company vault for {origin}
ask.balance.reading: Reading what the page sent. Nothing has been paid.
ask.balance.refused-title: This wallet will not pay for this
ask.balance.cannot-read: This wallet could not load what it reads a transaction with. Nothing has been paid.
ask.balance.leaves-why: Worked out from the transaction itself, not from anything the page said. The coins come from this wallet, and only from it.
ask.balance.no-fee: You pay no network fee. The company pays it.
ask.balance.public: The token and the amount above leave your public balance, and anyone reading the chain can see them, your wallet's public address, and the vault they went into.
ask.balance.night-stops-dust: NIGHT that goes into the vault no longer generates DUST for this wallet.
ask.balance.vault: The vault the transaction pays into: {vault}. This wallet cannot check that the vault belongs to that company.
ask.balance.compare: the person at this company who asked you to pay gave you themselves, and not through this page
ask.balance.paid: Once the company sends this transaction, the money is in its vault. Who can move it from there is decided by the company's account and its vault, not by this wallet, and nothing in this wallet can take it back.
ask.committee.headline: Change who holds a company's rules, for {origin}
ask.committee.hand-over: Brings the company's contracts to the committee that holds its account on the chain. No key joins the company this way.
ask.committee.super-admins: Changes who holds the company's contracts to the committee the page sends, every member of which has signed the change.
ask.committee.join: Signs, with your key, that you hold it, as one of the keys this change puts on the company's contracts. Nothing changes until enough of the super admins sign it too.
ask.committee.to: The committee after the change, as the page sends it: {count} keys, {threshold} of which must sign any change to the company's rules. Anyone not on it loses their place.
ask.committee.compare: the person who invited you to this company gave you themselves, and not through this page
ask.records-key.headline: Sign your records key for a company, for {origin}
ask.records-key.lede: Signs that your records key belongs to this company, for the seat you hold on its account. It names only the company, your records key and your seat, and cannot be used to change any of the company's rules.
ask.records-key.seat: Your seat, as the page names it: {seat}
ask.records-key.directory: In the same answer, your entry in the company's list of who files its records, signed with the key the page names: {key}
ask.records-key.compare-press: Approve only if the fingerprint matches. If this wallet has not kept an account for this company yet, approving keeps this one as the company's for good, and this wallet will sign for no other.
ask.records-key.compare: the person who invited you gave you themselves, by a call, a message or in person, and not through this page
ask.creation.headline: Finish creating a company, for {origin}
ask.creation.lede: Signs the step that finishes the company's account. This wallet reads the deploy the page built and checks it against its own build before it signs; if anything differs, nothing is signed.
ask.creation.held: The account is held by your own key for this company and by nobody else, from its first transaction. Signers you named do not hold it until its committee is changed to include them.
ask.creation.label: This wallet signs only for a company whose label it made up itself, and checks that after your passkey. The label the page gives for the company:
ask.join-code.headline: Make a code to join a company, for {origin}
ask.join-code.compare: the person adding you sees for the company, read out to you by a call, a message or in person, and not through this page
ask.addresses.headline: Show {origin} your wallet's private address and balances
ask.addresses.lede: The page sees this wallet's private address and balances, and nothing about your other wallets. Nothing is signed, and nothing can be paid with this. The page can keep what it sees. The page already has your public address from your sign-in, and anyone can read public amounts on the network.
ask.disclosure.headline: Share your details with {origin}
ask.join.headline: Accept the invitation from {origin}
ask.disclosure.lede: They ask for the details below. Your passkey opens this wallet; you then choose what is sent, and nothing leaves until you press Send.
ask.join.sealed: What you send is sealed on this device to this key before it leaves, and only whoever holds it can open it: {key}. This wallet cannot check the key belongs to the company you think you are joining.
ask.join-code.lede-signer: Signs a code saying that the keys for a seat on this company, as the page names them, are yours. Only their public halves are in the code; their secrets stay on the device that made them.
ask.join-code.lede-payee: Signs a code saying that you are paid at {address}, and that your payslips are sealed to the key this wallet gives for this company. Only these are in the code.
ask.join-code.person: You, as the page signed you in: {person}
ask.keyring.compare: the person who invited you to this company gave you themselves, and not through this page
ask.company-title: The company, as the page names it
ask.swapped-title: This is not the request you approved
ask.swapped: After your passkey, {origin} sent a different request from the one you approved in the window before it. It has been refused: nothing was signed, given or paid. If you meant to do something else, start it again from the page.
ask.committee.check: After your passkey, this wallet reads who holds each contract from the chain and shows you every key this change adds and removes. Nothing is signed until you press Sign this change there.
ask.passkey.none-here: {wallet} has no passkey kept in this browser, so no passkey was asked for: any passkey could have answered and opened another wallet. Nothing was opened and nothing was sent. Choose another wallet below, or open your wallet in a tab of its own, make a new passkey for it there or recover it from its pieces, then ask again from the page.
ask.passkey.other-wallet: That passkey opens another wallet held in this browser, not {wallet}. Nothing was opened and nothing was sent. Choose the wallet to answer with below, then use its passkey.
ask.balance.which-account: It is paid from the account of this wallet that this page has used before, or else from one no site has been given. Which one is kept in this wallet's sealed record, so it is named once your passkey opens the wallet. If another site also has that account's address, or no unused account is left, the payment waits there for you to choose.
ask.creation.after: The account the deploy creates, and its fingerprint, are shown after your passkey, when this wallet keeps that account as the company's.
